owner: Claude (Engineering Lead session of M10.1, Sonnet 5.5): wrote the oracle AND will write the implementation. Disclosed; independence comes from the reviewer, the pinned-before-implementation order, the protected files and the mutants below.
reviewer: A separate fresh-context Claude subagent (general-purpose, read-only, no test runs, no repository writes). It saw the draft oracle, the baseline code and the history of the two earlier oracles; no implementation existed. Full report: docs/reports/m10.1-oracle-review.md. It returned ORACLE_REJECTED for the first draft; the amendments below are the response.
authorization: The M10.1 mission prompt, Phase 4: 'Create a corrected acceptance specification for F2' and 'Use a separate reviewer or independently prepared deterministic oracle'. The same prompt authorises the Phase 2 and 3 cases and the not-ready budget amendment ('Review the historical M10 oracle versions').

lineage.note: M10, pinned before implementation; O-F2 asserted a handle-scoped engagedBy, which makes the scheduler's cross-resource cancel confirmation vacuous

M10, O-F2 amended to 'scope to the task's resource when known'; that fix produced a false STOPPED against http-boundary.test.ts:132 and was reverted; v2 case 'gemini task + unrelated codex permit -> stopped' contradicts the existing contract; its not-ready case (2.5 s) landed before the spawn under load

M10.1: O-F2 replaced by run-scoped ownership (16 cases + 3 guards), O-SA and O-PR added, O-FP/O-SM/O-RL carried; not-ready budget 15 s; lease-isolation must carry evidence of what it proves. Amendment reason: v2's O-F2 asserted behaviour that is itself unsafe; the operator's M10.1 mission specifies the corrected properties.

Type annotation only (`const copy: Record<string, any>`), required for `tsc --noEmit` to pass on the oracle file. No runtime change: node strips types. Made by the implementer before any candidate verdict, disclosed here; the baseline negative control was re-run on the new hash.

One case amended (O-SA: 'a reverted dependency does not satisfy its dependents'). As pinned it could not pass under ANY implementation: it moved a task READY->BACKLOG (illegal in the state machine), expected promote() to act on a READY task (promote only evaluates BACKLOG/BLOCKED), and its claim() assertion was vacuous because claim() only considers executor 'worker' tasks while the fixture used Claude-kept ones. Found by the implementer when the case failed with the implementation in place (error: 'READY -> BACKLOG is not allowed'); the independent reviewer missed it. The requirement (SA-c) is unchanged and now stronger: a real worker task must be unclaimable while its dependency is reverted and claimable again after reinstatement. The baseline negative control and the mutant control were re-run on the new hash. Disclosed: the amendment author is the implementer.

Operator-authorized PR #44 synchronization repair (2026-10-12). O-SM forced cases acknowledge the child fault/spawn ledger before advancing only ExecutionClock samples via a test-scoped mock; the real tick and all timeout/cancellation/permit assertions remain. The unforced 2.5 s wall-clock case is unchanged. Missing boundary evidence still fails, with the existing model budget bounding the wait. No production code changes. Targeted verification only; baseline/mutant and full regression are not claimed and remain operator review work. The before-spawn case injects a 3.5 s upstream delay, longer than the unchanged 2.5 s task budget, to deterministically reject the old startup race.

baselineMustFail: 1. same task id, different runs: each run is confirmed against its own permit only
2. same task id, different providers: a codex run does not block a gemini cancel, and the reverse
3. same task id, same provider: a sibling run's permit AND queue entry never block, a run's own always do
4. missing or default provider: a task with no provider is confirmed on its own permit, not a foreign one
5. injected handle / resource mismatch can neither hide the target's permit nor adopt a foreign one
9b. recovery: a re-run of the same task is not blocked by the previous run's stale permit, and the previous run still is
10b. an unreadable ownership marker is unknown ownership, not "some other run" (pins the holder syntax, see the header)
11. the Mastra workflow carries its own run id into the permit it takes (scheduler -> workflow run -> capacity)
12. overlapping run ids never match each other (whole-value comparison, not substring or prefix)
13. the runner's own retry takes a second permit for the SAME run, and that permit carries the run id too

14. scheduler -> executor -> workflow: the run id the scheduler stores is the one that owns the permit, so a foreign run of the same task never blocks the scheduler's own cancel and an unattributable permit still does
a DONE task whose implementation was reverted keeps its history and is not currently accepted; reinstating it restores acceptance
a revert needs a reason and a DONE task; nothing else is accepted
a reverted dependency does not satisfy its dependents, nothing can claim them, and reinstating it releases them
metrics do not count a reverted implementation as done, for either implementer, and report the revert
`lead tasks` shows the historical completion without claiming the code is still integrated
an objective recorded as ACCEPTED says a required task has since been reverted, keeps its history, and cannot be accepted again
promoting one objective mutates nothing in an unrelated objective
a BLOCKED task of another objective whose dependency has recovered is not released by someone else's promote either
an empty or unknown objective id is an error, never "global"
dependencies across objectives are read both ways: a scoped task sees a dead or finished dependency elsewhere
after the dependency is done, scoped promotion of its objective releases dependents in other objectives, transitively, and leaves strangers alone
history is append-only: earlier events are untouched by a scoped promotion
`lead plan` promotes the plan it created and nothing else (the M10 side effect)
declares the named boundaries
is inert without the explicit test enable, even when a plan is present (production cannot be affected)
when enabled: delays, can throw, logs one JSON line per firing, and an abort ends the delay at once
a plan naming an unknown boundary is refused, never silently ignored
timeout BEFORE the CLI is spawned: no provider process ever exists, no late spawn
timeout AFTER spawn but before the CLI is ready: the started group is killed although it never reported in
classifies the two known signatures and the environmental and unknown cases
